connections.observation: `s001` presents standing/moving as the first illustrative pair of opposites. `s003` recurs ἐναντίος throughout to mark the principle and its applications. `s019` opens with the proposal to determine sameness or difference and closes with the claim that the elements are διττά τε καὶ ἕτερα. The standing/moving opposition at the start becomes the template for the rational/desiring distinction at the end.

`s002` accumulates forms of αὐτός specifying sameness of subject, respect, and object in the principle statement. `s001` applies this to standing and moving κατὰ τὸ αὐτὸ ἅμα. `s006` enumerates paired opposites (nodding/shaking, reaching/refusing, drawing/pushing) each tested against the same formal requirement. The dense sameness-language establishes the strict conditions under which the paired opposites become evidence of plurality.

`s004` clusters spinning-top vocabulary: top, pivot, circle, straight, curved. `s005` enumerates four directions (right, left, forward, backward) as ways the axis might incline. Together they elaborate `s001`'s standing/moving opposition into a spatial figure where the straight axis stands while the circumference moves, and any directional tilt destroys the standing.

`s006` sets ἀπωθεῖσθαι (pushing away) opposite προσάγεσθαι (drawing toward) as abstract paired actions. `s010` recurs ἀπωθέω first in that abstract opposition, then applied to the soul's refusal, then to the archer's hands pushing the bow while the other pulls. The word moves from logical pair through psychic action to physical illustration.

`s007` densely recurs ἐπιθυμία/ἐπιθυμέω as desire is introduced and specified. `s008` clusters thirst, hunger, drink, food as the clearest bodily instances. `s009` pairs hot/cold and much/little as qualifications thirst-itself does not carry. The desire-vocabulary accumulates around the bodily appetites, which are then stripped of qualification to isolate desire as such.

`s008` clusters thirst, hunger, and their objects (drink, food). `s011` compares the desiring element to θηρίον—a beast—being led to drink. The bodily appetites specified in `s008` become the action attributed to the beast-image: the concrete thirst drives the comparison.

`s012` contrasts τὸ κελεῦον and τὸ κωλῦον as two presences in the soul. `s013` assigns the preventing element to λογισμός and the compelling element to παθήματα and νοσήματα. `s014` names the two λογιστικόν and ἀλόγιστον τε καὶ ἐπιθυμητικόν. The initial contrast between commanding and preventing becomes the sourced opposition of calculation versus affection, which receives the final names.

`s015` clusters the λογ- family (λογισμός, λογίζεται, λογιστικόν, ἀλόγιστον, ἀλόγως) at the naming moment. `s013` first introduces λογισμός as the source of restraint opposed to παθήματα. `s014` assigns λογιστικόν and ἀλόγιστον as the names. The lexical family accumulates densely where the rational part and its opposite receive their designations.

`s007` recurs ἐπιθυμία/ἐπιθυμέω densely. `s016` clusters ἐρᾷ, πεινῇ, διψῇ, ἐπτόηται, πληρώσεων, ἡδονῶν as characterizations of the desiring part. `s014` names that part ἀλόγιστον τε καὶ ἐπιθυμητικόν and lists those same verbs (ἐρᾷ, πεινῇ, διψῇ). The desire-vocabulary established throughout becomes the defining content of the named part.

`s010` recurs ἀπωθέω in three contexts: abstract opposition, psychic refusal, and the archer's hands pushing the bow. `s012` contrasts τὸ κελεῦον and τὸ κωλῦον as the commanding and preventing elements. The archer's two hands—one pushing, one pulling—enact the psychic opposition between the element that urges and the element that restrains.

`s018` passes μανθάνω between speakers: the interlocutor says οὐκ ἔμαθον, Socrates echoes οὐκ ἔμαθες, later asks εἰ ἄρα νῦν ἔμαθες, and receives ἔμαθον. `s019` opens with the proposal ἐπιχειρῶμεν αὐτὰ ὁρίζεσθαι and closes with ἀξιώσομεν αὐτὰ διττά τε καὶ ἕτερα ἀλλήλων εἶναι. The understanding-vocabulary marks stages in the proof, and its completion coincides with the fulfillment of the opening proposal to determine sameness or difference.

`s001` sets standing and moving as the first opposition. `s004` elaborates this with the spinning-top, whose straight axis stands while its curved part moves. `s010` applies ἀπωθέω to the archer's hands, one pushing the bow away while the other draws it near. The section presents three physical illustrations—person, top, archer—each demonstrating simultaneous opposites in different parts of the same thing.

`s009` pairs hot/cold and much/little as qualifications that thirst does not inherently possess. `s008` clusters thirst and hunger with their objects (drink, food). The qualifications are proposed, then stripped away to isolate thirst as desire for drink as such, not for qualified drink: the movement strips appetite to its bare relation to its object.

`s011` compares the desiring element to θηρίον being led to drink. `s017` calls the same element ἑταῖρον—companion—of fillings and pleasures. The desiring part receives two relational images: beast being led and companion of pleasures, one emphasizing compulsion, the other association.

`s012` places τὸ κελεῦον and τὸ κωλῦον as two presences in the soul, one urging drinking and the other preventing it. `s013` assigns the preventing element to λογισμός and the compelling element to παθήματα καὶ νοσήματα. The initial dramatic contrast (commanding versus preventing) receives its causal grounding (calculation versus affections and ailments).

elements.context: ταὐτὸν τἀναντία ... κατὰ ταὐτόν γε καὶ πρὸς ταὐτὸν οὐκ ἐθελήσει ἅμα (436b); τὸ αὐτὸ ἅμα κατὰ τὸ αὐτὸ (436c); ἅμα κατὰ τὸ αὐτὸ πρὸς τὸ αὐτὸ (437a); ἅμα περιφερόμενον (436e); τἀναντία πράττοι (439b); αἱ χεῖρες τὸ τόξον ἀπωθοῦνταί τε καὶ προσέλκονται (439b)

new_signals.observation: ἅμα (simultaneously, at the same time) recurs as the temporal condition that makes opposites impossible in the same subject: the principle requires that opposites not occur ἅμα, and each illustration tests simultaneity.

elements.context: αὐτὴ ἡ ἐπιθυμία ἑκάστη αὐτοῦ μόνον ἑκάστου οὗ πέφυκεν (437e); αὐτὰ μὲν μόνα αὐτῶν μόνων ἐστίν (438d); αὐτὸ δίψος πέφυκεν (439a)

new_signals.observation: The intensive αὐτό construction recurs to isolate each desire or relation as such, stripped of qualification: desire-itself for its object-itself, not for qualified objects.

elements.context: ποιοῦ τινος πώματος ποιόν τι καὶ δίψος (439a); ποιοῦ τινος ποιά τις (438d-e); occurs eight times in 437d-439a

new_signals.observation: ποῖος (of what sort, qualified) recurs densely in the argument distinguishing qualified relations from unqualified ones: what is ποιόν τι relates to ποιοῦ τινος, while the thing itself relates to its object itself.

elements.context: οὐδεὶς ποτοῦ ἐπιθυμεῖ ἀλλὰ χρηστοῦ ποτοῦ, καὶ οὐ σίτου ἀλλὰ χρηστοῦ σίτου. πάντες γὰρ ἄρα τῶν ἀγαθῶν ἐπιθυμοῦσιν

new_signals.observation: An objection is voiced: no one desires drink but good drink, food but good food, since all desire good things. The objection introduces χρηστός and ἀγαθός as qualifications that would make all desire inherently qualified.
